=== MISSED 1 ===
WHAT: The exhausted-retry failure path (`log.warn(`webhook ${event} not delivered after ${delays.length + 1} attempts`)` in src/webhooks.js) is not changed to include the new `delivery` id. Combined with the already-confirmed facts that nothing about a delivery is persisted anywhere (silent-drops/data-integrity) and this log line is the sole server-side trace of a specific failed delivery, this is the one moment a human actually needs the id this PR introduces: to tell a receiver's support team 'which delivery was this' when triaging a drop. The feature's own purpose (a stable identifier for correlating one event across two systems) is undermined on exactly the unhappy path where correlation matters.
WHY: 'security' only checked that this same log line doesn't leak the secret, not whether it should carry the new id. 'silent-drops'/'data-integrity' confirmed nothing is persisted, but concluded that meant no finding, without following through to 'therefore this log line is the only record, and it's missing the key field.' No angle treats operator-facing observability of the new feature as its own subsystem.

=== MISSED 2 ===
WHAT: The new test's UUID-shape assertion, `assert.match(ids[0], /^[0-9a-f-]{36}$/)`, doesn't actually enforce UUID structure — confirmed with a quick node check that a 36-character string of a single repeated hex digit and no dashes at all (`'a'.repeat(36)`) also matches it. The scout's mutation test (moving `randomUUID()` into the retry loop) only exercised the 'same id across retries' assertions (`ids[0] === ids[1]`, `ids[1] !== ids[2]`); it never exercised this third assertion. A future change that swapped `randomUUID()` for some other 36-char hex/dash id scheme with the wrong internal structure would pass this test silently.
WHY: 'tests-that-dont-test' verified non-vacuousness only for the id-reuse behavior via one targeted mutation; it didn't check each of the test's three assertions independently, so the weak regex on the third assertion was never exercised by that verification.

=== MISSED 3 ===
WHAT: `deliver()`'s new local `const delivery = randomUUID()` (a string) and `notify()`'s pre-existing `const delivery = deliver(event, data).finally(...)` (a Promise) now share the identifier `delivery` for two unrelated values in nested scopes of the same small file. It causes no bug today, but it's a trap for the next person who touches this function and conflates the two.
WHY: The 'correctness' angle looks for behavioral defects, not naming hygiene; a shadowing pair with no current runtime effect falls outside every listed angle's checklist even though it's a direct, visible consequence of this diff's choice of variable name.
